subject: Reactive Timers for Partial render - how?

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: Reactive Timers for Partial render - how?
parts:
Suppose I have a graph which takes 2 seconds to render.

Suppose I could generate a partial graph (say, take sample() of the data, or similar) which takes 0.1 seconds to render and send.

If the user is dragging a picker, interactivity will be poor if the 2 second graph is called each time, but okay with 0.1 seconds.

Additionally, the requests may build up as the slider is pulled around, causing a series of graphs to be displayed in turn after the slider action ends with nothing the bewildered user can do to stop it.  (rather like the slowing of time that is experienced when leaving ones keys inside the car and closing the door).

I see there is a reactive timer; how might we use it in the following design?:

renderGraph() {
  if (!timerExpired) {
    plot(input$slider*sample(100,dataset))
    resetTimer(300*ms)
  } else {
    plot(input$slider*dataset)
  }
}

So for the following inputs

1, 2, 3, 4, 5 each 100s apart, it would render the subsampled graph 5 times, and after 300ms after the last one, the renderGraph would be invalidated and the full res graph uploaded.

This looks a bit like invalidateLater, except that I need to know for a given render function if the timer has been invalided or not yet, so as to decide which graph to draw, and I need to be able to reset it (and maybe clear it too).

-Alex

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Reactive Timers for Partial render - how?
parts:
Our current (simplistic) approach to this problem has been to do "debouncing" and "throttling" on the client side, on the input bindings (getRatePolicy). One work item we have is to make this setting configurable on a per-input basis, so you could increase the debounce/throttle interval if you know a particular input will trigger an expensive recalculation.

That doesn't, however, solve the issue of partial rendering/subsampling. If that's really important to you then maybe this would work:

lastKnownSliderValue <- NULL
renderPlot({
  if (!identical(input$slider, lastKnownSliderValue)) {
    lastKnownSliderValue <- input$slider
    invalidateLater(300)
    plot(input$slider*sample(100,dataset))
  } else {
    plot(input$slider*dataset)
  }
})

Could be wrapped up with an API like this:

renderPlot({
  debouncedPlot(
    300,     # millisecond threshold
    {input$slider},     # explicitly provide inputs--wrap in a list() if more than one
    {plot(input$slider*sample(100, dataset))},     # Cheap version
    {plot(input$slider*dataset)}     # Expensive version
  )
})
